text: A proof of concept for eligibility, agreement preparation, review, and electronic signature
AI Clinic project review and handoff
Introduce the project as a working proof of concept for Innovation Partnerships. The deck covers the problem, design reasoning, current workflow, and handoff recommendations.
Repeated review and document handling created avoidable work
The same facts moved between the questionnaire, checklist, Word templates, and email. Each transfer created another opportunity for inconsistent routing or copied values.
Automate routine standard requests while preserving legal rules, document review, and a staff-review route for exceptions.
U-M Innovation Partnerships | Outgoing MTA automation
The department already had a process, but staff carried out the repeatable steps manually. The design target was the standard path, not every possible exception.
The supplied materials defined the workflow; institutional ownership remains a next-phase decision

The team treated the supplied documents as authoritative source material. The next phase needs named owners for the institutional services and operating decisions around the workflow.
A hybrid design matched the legal and technical risk
Clear decisions, but weak handling of open-text evidence and wording variation.
Flexible language handling, but unsafe for final legal eligibility decisions.
Checklist rules decide eligibility. A local language model supports only open-text evidence that needs interpretation.
Reason: the checklist stays explainable and testable, while the language model reduces dependence on hard-coded phrases.
U-M Innovation Partnerships | Outgoing MTA automation
The system deliberately keeps policy in deterministic code. The language model supports specific evidence questions and never chooses the agreement or approves an exception.
The backend separates intake, policy, documents, review, and delivery
Staff review remains available whenever a rule fails, evidence stays unresolved, or no approved automated template applies.
U-M Innovation Partnerships | Outgoing MTA automation
The review gate matters. The system never sends an agreement directly from the questionnaire without showing the values and generated document first.
The checklist controls the decision; a local language model handles bounded text evidence

Local language model
for open text
“Research in the chemistry class” does not establish that a chemical will not be used in humans. The condition stays unresolved.
Model risk: false positives can contribute to an unsafe approval. False negatives send valid requests to staff review. Thresholds therefore favor avoiding false positives.
U-M Innovation Partnerships | Outgoing MTA automation

Structured answers remain primary. The local facebook/bart-large-mnli model supports permitted open-text evidence and records entailment, contradiction, and neutral scores. Production evaluation must measure false positives and false negatives for each checklist condition.
Material category selects an approved template only after eligibility passes
Each template has its own tested population strategy. Production UBMTA routing should also verify organization participation and signer authority from a trusted source.
U-M Innovation Partnerships | Outgoing MTA automation

The proof of concept maps biological materials to UBMTA and animal-derived materials to the AUTM biological agreement. A production service should add authoritative UBMTA organization and signer verification before delivery.

The verified suite covers intake, rules, model decision handling through controlled doubles, template selection, rendering, review, signing plans, SignNow payloads, references, and interface behavior.
Confirm production deliverables, acceptance criteria, ownership, and support before launch.
Agreement files use different structures, field labels, optional terms, and signer layouts.
The active biological route still needs authoritative organization participation and signer data for production.
Assign owners for authentication, hosting, website integration, records, and database services.
Confirm rules, signature authority, retention, and the staff-review route with all responsible offices.
Future staffing needs strong backend and architecture capability, document testing, AI evaluation, and ongoing legal and process ownership.
The next phase should treat the operating model as seriously as the code
U-M Innovation Partnerships | Outgoing MTA automation
These are the decisions required to move from a verified workflow to a supported institutional service. They do not change the core intake, eligibility, agreement, review, and signing design.
Build on the existing backend instead of restarting the workflow
Name policy, template, IT, security, records, and support owners.
Control versions, population markers, formatting, and signature blocks.
Implement U-M login, roles, a database, and approved document storage.
Use verified SignNow events to retrieve, checksum, store, and reconcile final records.
Verify organization participation and authorized signers from a trusted institutional source.
Add evidence highlighting, contradiction checks, review suggestions, document-quality checks, and staff-case summaries with measured error rates and human confirmation.
A secure standalone MTA service with persistent, searchable signed records

The next phase should preserve the verified intake, rules, routing, population, review, and signing modules. Production work should add institutional identity, records, hosting, monitoring, and ownership. AI should remain assistive and should be evaluated against labeled examples before any production use.
